title: Linearity of the combined vector
statement: Let $n,m$ be nonnegative integers, let $f_1,f_2:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, let $g_1,g_2$ be $m$-tuples of real-valued functions on $\{0,1\}^n$, let $c,d\in\mathbb R$, and let $x\in\{0,1\}^n$. The combined vector of the linear combinations $cf_1+df_2$ and $cg_1+dg_2$ at $x$ is $c$ times the combined vector of $(f_1,g_1)$ at $x$ plus $d$ times the combined vector of $(f_2,g_2)$ at $x$.
hypotheses_covered: f₁,f₂ are real-valued functions on the n-dimensional Boolean cube
g₁,g₂ are m-tuples of real-valued functions on that cube
x is a point of the n-dimensional Boolean cube
replaced: For a profile $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, a real function $h$ on a uniform Boolean cube, and a vector $k$ of real functions on that cube, put $V(h,k)(x)=((D_i h(x))_i,(k_j(x))_j)$ and $F_P(h,k)=\mathbb E\sqrt{P(h)^2+\|V(h,k)\|_2^2}$, where $D_i$ is the coordinate half-difference. For real $c,d$, functions $f_1,f_2$ on the cube, and vectors $g_1,g_2$ of $m$ cube functions, $V(cf_1+df_2,cg_1+dg_2)(x)=cV(f_1,g_1)(x)+dV(f_2,g_2)(x)$ for every $x$.
